tagline: Catch the waste. Close the risk. Before the bill arrives.
welcome1: Scans your AWS account read-only for wasted money and security risks.
welcome2: Explains every finding in plain words and forecasts your month-end bill.
welcome3: Never changes anything without your typed confirmation.
scan_error: Could not scan. Check your AWS credentials and permissions.
empty: Nothing here yet. Run a scan or try Demo Mode.
no_ce: Cost Explorer data is not available, so no bill forecast can be made. Waste found by scans: {amount}/month (estimate).
sim_hint: Tick the findings you plan to fix.
plan_hint: Biggest risk and savings first. Tick when done.
real_off: Real actions are off. Turn them on in Settings (Live mode only).
set_rate: USD to INR rate (your assumption, not live)
set_bedrock: Use Amazon Bedrock for explanations (may cost money)
set_real_hint: Type ENABLE to allow real actions.
disclaimer: Security notice: BillShield is read-only by default. Review every command before you run it.
translation_note: AI-assisted translations: please have a native speaker review them.
pdf_note: The PDF report is in English (PDF fonts for Indian scripts are not bundled).
ask_hint: Answers come only from your own findings.
q_score: Why is my score what it is?
ans_high: Most waste comes from {rtype}: about {amount}/month across {n} resource(s) (estimate).
ans_save: Fixing all cost findings could save about {amount}/month (estimate).
ans_score: Health score {score}/100: waste penalty {wp}, security risk penalty {rp}.
ans_none: No findings yet, so there is nothing to answer from.
fact_none: No recurring cost; this is a security risk.
suggest: Review the dry-run command first. Fix it only if you are sure you no longer need it.
why_ec2: A stopped server still pays for its attached disks until you delete them.
why_ebs: A disk not attached to any server keeps billing every month.
why_eip: An Elastic IP that is not in use is billed by the hour.
why_snap: Old snapshots keep billing for storage and are often forgotten.
why_nat: A NAT gateway bills every hour even when no traffic passes through it.
why_sg: Remote-login ports open to the whole internet are constantly probed by attackers.
why_s3: A public bucket can expose your files to anyone on the internet.
why_iam: Without MFA, a stolen password is enough to take over the account.
s1_checks: Stopped servers, unattached disks, unused IPs, old snapshots, NAT gateways, public S3 buckets, open SSH/RDP ports, users without MFA.
s1_never: It never changes, deletes or stops anything on its own. It never saves your keys. Real actions need your typed confirmation.
keys_note: Keys stay in memory for this browser session only. They are never saved or logged. Use a read-only IAM user, never the root account.
conn_fail: Could not connect. Check the profile name or keys.
bad_key: That access key ID does not look valid.
root_warn: This is the ROOT account. Create a read-only IAM user first, then connect with that.
